create.name: Tim Freke
create.bio:
Tim Freke is an English philosopher and writer who has spent his life exploring the world's spiritual traditions, a search he traces back to an experience of awakening at the age of twelve. He has written some thirty-five books, among them a Sunday Times bestseller, and for decades has led events in many countries, often presenting himself as a stand-up philosopher who mixes humour with serious questions about life and death. In 2013 he decided that much of his earlier thinking about spirituality needed rebuilding, and he set out to develop a new evolutionary approach.

He calls this approach Unividualism: the idea that awakening is not the dissolving of the self but its growth into a person who feels at one with the universe while remaining fully individual. Central to his teaching is what he calls psysensing, simple practices for sensing oneness and sensing other people directly, which participants try together in pairs and groups. He shares much of his philosophy freely on his YouTube channel, through the long-running What Is Life? conversations and the chapter-by-chapter talks of his podbook Why Your Life Really Matters. In person he leads Big Weekends in Glastonbury, where his wife Deborah adds sensory and movement meditations, and he hosts an online community for people who want to keep exploring together.
